newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi to return to skies with low fares, fewer jets.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi to return to skies with low fares, fewer jets.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines said Thursday it will return to scheduled service later this month with one-way fares of $79 and $99 from Newark, N.J., to Chicago, Atlanta and West Palm Beach.

Though Kiwi has not won final approval to start flying again from the Federal Aviation Administration, its chief executive, Jerry Murphy, said he was confident the airline will resume operations with seven aircraft and about 450 to 500 employees.
At its peak, Kiwi had 15 aircraft and 1,200 employees. It halted operations in October after filing for bankruptcy-law protection from creditors in September.
"Many so-called experts have written off this airline from the beginning ... but I think we have proven that if a cat has nine lives, a Kiwi has at least 10," Murphy said.
While Kiwi won $5 million in new financing in November and is working on securing up to $15 million in additional capital, some industry analysts said they doubt Kiwi has enough capital to thrive.
Kiwi declined to say when it will emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy, but said it will expand service slowly. Kiwi plans to resume scheduled service on Jan. 20.
The airline also said it was in talks to buy newer aircraft and that it was weighing marketing arrangements with some domestic and international carriers.
While it declined to comment on the aircraft it may buy, it said it is looking for short-haul jets.
"We are a niche carrier, we expect to stay a niche carrier. We will not be operating internationally," Murphy said.
Kiwi said it made 500 bookings since announcing its plan Thursday morning. The new fares are unrestricted and can be booked by calling the airline or a travel agent.
